keyFindings.description: With a broker that sends no approve_url (every state where Dispatch carries step 1 and the broker does not: rollout step 2 moves Dispatch first, a failed A13 pre-check, a broker rollback) the secret-request Inbox row is an unlinked div 'Decided on the secrets broker.' and nothing links /credentials/<record>, the only place an old broker's request can be decided. Breaks spec rollout step 1 and A12 ('the row keeps today's link'). inbox.e2e.ts:993-1022 and CredentialRequestsSection.test.tsx:66-77 pin the wrong behaviour.
waitingOn with no approve_url no longer prints <AGENT_SECRETS_APPROVE_URL>/credentials/<record>; spec A12/design: 'until step 3, when the broker sends no approve_url, it prints what it prints today'.

The page lacks the two sentences the spec's 'What the page shows' and A1 require (what Approve gives, with the lifetime; what Deny and expiry do), and prints 'none given' where the spec says 'No reason given'. No test asserts them.

TestABrokerItCannotReachNamesNoCredentialTheURLCarries still runs the removed `approve` subcommand and fails at this head (reproduced: exit 2 'unknown subcommand "approve"'); no test pins the new usage or the refusal of approve/deny.
end-sessions only trims its login; sessions are stored lowercased, so `end-sessions Ada@Example.com` deletes 0 rows and exits 0 while Ada keeps deciding up to 24 h. Use record.CanonicalLogin.

The dispatch filter names no broker package, though run-broker.sh builds cmd/broker, cmd/dev-oidc-issuer and brokertest/requestseed and broker-approval.e2e.ts is the only proof of A5's browser half and A6; a broker-only change skips it. ci_job_reads.py does not model run-broker.sh, so check-ci-filters passes anyway.

Page.codeFlow holds p.mu across a network Discover and rebuilds the CodeFlow after a failure, defeating oidc's singleflight and 5 s failure spacing: during an issuer outage page loads and callbacks serialize, each up to 10 s.
A11's rollback clause ('the broker binary from the commit before step 1 starts against a database that step 1 migrated'; plan D12 and the A11 row) has no recorded run.
A7's last clause ('Dispatch's machine-login page still finds and decides it in Dispatch's browser suite') has no browser test; only a heading check exists (two-builds.multiprocess.e2e.ts:446).
parseSignIn reads settings by index into the exported mutable SignInSettings slice.
Exchange still returns an anonymous error with ErrNonce's exact text.
ApproveURL *string for a field the broker sends as string,omitempty.
Package doc (:10) and ApplyDecision doc (:594) still say a Dispatch login decides a secret request.

The approval page and sign-in routes spend no per-address bucket: an unauthenticated caller drives a record read per GET /approve/<id> and, with a sign-in cookie it got from that GET, a token request to the provider and a last_failed_sign_in write per GET /signin/callback.
